finding: At modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk@4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, TaskAckResult is the empty tasks/update and tasks/cancel acknowledgement: it serializes resultType=complete with optional _meta omitted by default, and ServerResult::task_ack(()) constructs TaskAckResult::new(). In the stock TaskManager cancel_task path, the manager first resolves the task, sets cancel_requested=true, sends the cooperative cancel signal, clears pending input requests for nonterminal tasks, touches the task and recomputes its status; only then does cancel_task return Ok(()). The source explicitly says this records cancellation intent and acknowledges immediately: after the request the task leaves input_required and reports working until the operation settles. Combining this slice with parent revision86's exact handler/server.rs evidence that successful ServerHandler::cancel_task is mapped to ServerResult::task_ack, a successful wire acknowledgement proves receipt/materialization of cancellation intent, not terminal cancellation or cessation of the underlying effect. An authenticated-owner gate therefore must run before application cancellation; a post-ack client must use tasks/get to observe eventual terminal state, and external-effect duplicate/late-completion safety remains a separate unresolved obligation.

No compile/runtime experiment was run in this slice; conclusions are source-level plus parent source-qualified handler evidence.
